_comment: Accepted SAST findings that are allowed to remain outstanding. Each entry needs a dated, reasoned rationale - see docs/REQUIREMENTS.md R1, which this file backs. Adding an entry here silences scripts/mobsfscan_check.py / scripts/mobsf_summary.py for that specific finding only; it does not disable the underlying scan.

mobsfscan.android_task_hijacking2: 2026-09-09: known tool limitation, not a real vulnerability - mobsfscan flags a task-affinity/launch-mode pattern generically, without the runtime context to distinguish it from this app's actual (safe) configuration. See docs/REQUIREMENTS.md R1.

mobsf.App can be installed on a vulnerable unp: 2026-09-09: restates this project's own deliberate minSdk=24 choice, not a new risk - lowering minSdk further is not currently planned. See CLAUDE.md's toolchain table and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md R1.
mobsf.Broadcast Receiver (com.crescendoalarm.c: 2026-09-24: DirectBootReceiver must be exported=true for the OS to deliver LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED at all (T-158) - an unexported receiver gets no broadcast. LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED is itself a protected-broadcast action (AOSP frameworks/base core/res/AndroidManifest.xml: '<protected-broadcast android:name="android.intent.action.LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED" />', verified against current AOSP source, same protection BOOT_COMPLETED itself relies on) - the platform rejects any attempt by a third-party app to send it with a SecurityException; only system/platform-signed code can originate it, and no app-declared android:permission could add anything on top of an OS-enforced sender-side check that cannot be targeted by app code at all. The receiver also reads no data from the Intent beyond its action string; the due time it acts on comes only from its own device-protected SharedPreferences (DirectBootFallback.getDueAt), writable only by this app's own code. Worst case under a hypothetical bypass (itself requiring platform-signature/system privilege) is an early, bounded, non-destructive 10-minute fallback siren using the system's own default alarm sound - no data access, no privilege escalation. Independently reviewed under CLAUDE.md's Philipp (security-researcher) persona; this WARNING-severity finding was never release-gating under R1's own high-or-above bar, and this entry exists for the documented rationale, not to unblock anything. See docs/TODO.md T-160. Package renamed 2026-09-25 from com.wakeywakey.wakeywakey to com.crescendoalarm.crescendoalarm (Crescendo Alarm rename) - this key updated to match, same underlying finding and rationale.
